regime_context: Detector shows a narrow, non-directional rotation concentrated in four eligible Hong Kong themes, led by Banks (crowded, mean-revert, wide breadth) with Energy as the only strong challenger; momentum is a focus lens only and the validated edge is the absolute-trend gate (which does help here). Given weak cross-sectional rank-IC and the mean-revert tag on the leader, I default to low conviction across the board and avoid any directional certainty.

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the only non-crowded eligible theme with a positive trend tag (hurst=trend, durability 0.72) and rank 2. It is the clearest challenger to Banks, with the rotation margin narrowing to 0.465 and absorption only 0.44, suggesting leadership is not yet consolidated. I lean in the direction the trend-gate and durability legs permit, while noting the narrow eligible pool (4 of 17) means this is a low-conviction structural lean, not a momentum call.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks are the crowded leader (crowding_z 1.16) with a mean-revert hurst tag despite rank 1 and very wide breadth (0.923). The guardrails explicitly say not to fade the leader on crowding and not to use it as a buy list, but positioning INTO the most crowded name with a mean-revert tag offers poor risk-reward for a fresh lean; the absolute-trend gate's risk-control edge argues for not adding here. I frame this as an avoid on a fresh allocation basis, not a short or sell.
